correctness.rationale: Every five-bit candidate x produces exactly seven distinct six-bit insertion outputs, while every six-bit target must be covered by a five-bit predecessor from its six deletion positions. Branching on every possible predecessor of one uncovered target is logically exhaustive; pruning if uncovered count exceeds 7 times remaining chosen centers cannot remove an actual solution. Independently implemented a different bitset DFS on all 32 candidate centers and all 64 targets, ruled out 11 or fewer centers and enumerated six distinct size-12 codebooks; the six optima match the three displayed representatives and their complements/reversals. The independent enumeration used 13,351 nodes; the two repository verifiers use independent branching orders. This is a complete finite-domain proof, not sampled extrapolation.
